claims.claim_en: A compact class-oriented response representation supports selective acceptance without changing the detector prediction or retraining its image representation.
claims.support: Nine features, nine coefficients and one intercept; train-only scaler; original deterministic class retained.
claims.limit: The scaler has additional stored statistics; six detector views dominate cost. This is not a new transformation-confidence principle.

claims.claim_en: The frozen full selector improves error ranking and matched-coverage error counts over ordinary confidence on the original external cohorts.
claims.evidence_level: original external evaluation; OF primary, DS secondary
claims.support: AURC reductions of 39.40% and 20.33%; matched errors 66 vs. 97 and 675 vs. 746, with stored paired group intervals for the risk differences.
claims.limit: Known-source cohorts and fixed checkpoints; does not restore the2% target under OpenFake shift.

claims.claim_en: The full selector retains fewer errors than all three Bahat-style runs at both original matched coverages.
claims.support: DeepShield: 66 vs. 81/80/81 errors at 9,807 accepted. OpenFake: 675 vs. 710/712/712 errors at 3,639 accepted.
claims.limit: No CI at these exact coverages. Do not call all six matched-count differences statistically significant.

claims.claim_en: At 95% coverage the full selector improves on every Bahat-style run on both cohorts, with all six paired pointwise intervals strictly favoring full.
claims.support: DeepShield: 18 vs. 29/31/28 errors. OpenFake: 747 vs. 795/792/790 errors. All six 5,000-replicate risk intervals are negative.
claims.limit: Pointwise unadjusted intervals, fixed models; no familywise or every-coverage superiority claim.

claims.claim_en: With architecture and training procedure held constant, the proposed degradation family improves the error-ranking inputs to the learned reference.
claims.support: Mean AURC reductions of 20.84% on DeepShield and 13.41% on OpenFake across three seeds; all six seed-specific paired AURC intervals are negative.
claims.limit: No pooled CI for the across-seed mean; evidence specific to the fixed detector, samples and implementation.

claims.claim_en: Class orientation and the half-size response make measurable positive contributions in the exploratory feature controls.
claims.support: Removing orientation gives 84/698 errors instead of 66/675. Removing the half-size response gives 84/740. Paired AURC intervals favor full in both cohorts.
claims.limit: Does not establish that every transformation or summary is necessary; resize-only point estimates can improve full.

claims.claim_en: The compact profile provides complementary error-ranking evidence beyond native-head MC dropout and native-logit energy.
claims.support: Both AURC contrasts favor full on DeepShield and OpenFake with negative 95% intervals; 95%-coverage errors are 18 vs. 43/40 and 747 vs. 809/808.
claims.limit: Specific trained dropout head and fixed entropy/energy definitions; timings are not directly comparable.

claims.claim_en: The advantage over ordinary confidence extends to two additional frozen detector pipelines.
claims.evidence_level: new external sample; predeclared OpenFake conjunction
claims.support: Both CLIP and ResNet-50 primary upper 95% bounds are below zero; all six detector-by-dataset confidence AURC contrasts are favorable.
claims.limit: Selectors are refitted separately; architecture, source training and preprocessing differ; absolute accuracy is poor and CLIP learned-confidence exception remains.

claims.claim_en: A separately assessed frozen acceptance rule reaches high coverage while meeting its prespecified same-distribution risk bound.
claims.support: 1,958/2,000 accepted (97.9%); 13 errors (0.66394%); one-sided 95% upper bound 1.05353%, below the 2% target.
claims.limit: Requires independent representative observations and unchanged target mixture; not guaranteed under distribution shift.

claims.claim_en: The study turns a promising post-hoc simplification into a transparent predeclared replacement decision on new data.
claims.evidence_level: independent audited ablation confirmation with conditional limitations
claims.support: 7,500 new images; four primary conditions; only OpenFake AURC passes; the full selector is retained without reinterpreting secondary findings.
claims.limit: A validation-protocol contribution, not proof that full is best or that resize has no benefit.

necessary_counterevidence: Transformation-response confidence is established by Bahat and Shakhnarovich; do not claim its invention.
Exact original coverage matched-error improvements versus Bahat have no stored CIs; the six strictly negative risk CIs refer to 95% coverage only.
All Bahat, transformation-family, feature-ablation and MC/energy comparisons reuse the same 14000 external images; they are retrospective.

The Bahat seed-43 adaptation has better OpenFake AURC; a matched-view nonlinear MLP over oriented margins also improves OpenFake AURC over full. Neither reverses the observed high-coverage advantage of full.
A learned confidence-only model has lower CLIP/OpenFake AURC than full; no stored direct full-versus-learned-confidence CI exists.
Nine features are not proved necessary; resize-only and removing summaries/confidence can improve some ranking outcomes.
The 7500-image resize confirmation passes only OpenFake AURC, not the replacement rule; retain_full is not evidence of full superiority.
OpenFake group imbalance, missing historical pHash, known-source sampling and unknown pretraining overlap limit independence and uncertainty interpretation.
The calibrated 2% target is a same-distribution fixed-rule result, not a certificate for shifted cohorts. External OpenFake selected risk remains about 18.55%.
All evaluated tasks remain binary real/synthetic classification. This is multi-detector evidence, not multiclass evidence or controlled architectural causality.
Ten logistic parameters establish scorer compactness, not measured end-to-end speed superiority; full requires six detector views and MC uses a cached backbone.

contributions: We develop a compact selector that expresses JPEG and resizing responses as class-oriented margin changes and nonlinear summaries. Nine logistic coefficients and one intercept determine acceptance while the original detector prediction and image representation remain fixed.

We isolate the contribution of the transformation family through matched-model controls. Replacing the reference transformations with the proposed degradations reduces mean AURC by 20.84% on DeepShield and 13.41% on OpenFake; all six seed-specific paired intervals favor the proposed views. At 95% coverage, the full selector also retains fewer errors than each of three Bahat-style runs on both cohorts.

We demonstrate complementary error-ranking value against ordinary confidence, native-head MC dropout and native-logit energy, and reproduce the primary advantage over ordinary confidence in separately fitted CLIP and ResNet-50 selection pipelines.

We connect ranking evaluation to a frozen acceptance rule assessed on a separate sample, then independently test a cheaper ablation using a locked replacement criterion. This separates reproducible operational gains from improvements that remain exploratory or insufficient for replacement.
proposed_english.discussion: The central empirical contribution is a practical high-coverage advantage from a compact error-ranking model. At the original matched acceptance counts, the full selector retains 66 rather than 80–81 errors on DeepShield and 675 rather than 710–712 on OpenFake across the three Bahat-style runs. At 95% coverage, the advantage is also supported by all six paired pointwise intervals, with 18 rather than 28–31 errors on DeepShield and 747 rather than 790–795 on OpenFake. A second contribution concerns the views themselves: keeping the learned reference architecture and training procedure fixed, our degradations reduce mean AURC by 20.84% and 13.41%. Thus, the evidence supports both a useful operating point for the compact selector and the choice of transformation family. These are retrospective comparisons and do not imply universal ranking superiority: the Bahat seed-43 model and the MLP over oriented margins achieve better OpenFake AURC. This distinction strengthens the practical interpretation by identifying where the compact selector is advantageous and where a different ranking model remains preferable.
proposed_english.abstract: Synthetic-image detectors can make confident errors under distribution shift. We develop a compact selective classifier that uses transformation responses to accept a frozen detector's original prediction or abstain. Nine features combine the original margin magnitude, five class-oriented changes under JPEG compression and resizing, and three response summaries. On DeepShield and OpenFake, the full logistic selector reduces area under the risk–coverage curve relative to confidence by 39.40% and 20.33%. At 95% coverage it retains 18 rather than 28–31 errors on DeepShield and 747 rather than 790–795 on OpenFake across three Bahat-style runs; all six retrospective paired pointwise intervals favor the full selector. Matched-model controls additionally support the degradation family, reducing mean AURC by 20.84% and 13.41% while holding the reference network architecture and training procedure fixed. Retrospective comparisons also favor the profile over native-head Monte Carlo dropout and native-logit energy. The primary improvement over ordinary confidence extends to CLIP and ResNet-50 pipelines, although absolute accuracy and learned-reference exceptions limit the claim. A separate frozen-rule assessment reaches 97.9% coverage with a one-sided 95% risk bound of 1.054% under its same-distribution assumptions. Finally, a 7,500-image independent test of a cheaper resizing ablation satisfies only one of four replacement conditions. The results establish useful high-coverage and transformation-family gains without claiming uniform superiority or distribution-independent risk control.
